historical_claim_wording: Instruction tuning degrades error recovery performance in language models (D = -0.21, p < 0.05).
original_scientific_flaw: Derived from Protocol 1.0 where 83% of Base Control rollouts were truncated at 64 tokens and Control prompts lacked Step 1 context.
empirical_evidence_status: CONTRADICTED by Protocol 2.0 where Base and Instruct both show 0% recovery (D = -0.03 under heuristic parser, D = 0.00 under semantic parser).
falsification_assessment: FALSIFIED. The negative interaction does not replicate under state-matched prompting with adequate token budgets.
scientifically_defensible_replacement: Under state-matched continuation prompting, neither base nor instruct checkpoints exhibit spontaneous recovery (p_BR = p_IR = 0.000), yielding no significant interaction contrast (D = 0.0000, p = 1.000).

historical_claim_wording: The historical negative interaction was entirely an artifact of prompt unbalancing and truncation.
original_scientific_flaw: Overstates causal attribution when multiple experimental variables (token budget, prompt syntax, boundary cue, verifier) were modified simultaneously.
empirical_evidence_status: METHODOLOGICALLY CONFOUNDED. Protocol 1.0 and 2.0 differ across at least 4 concurrent dimensions.
falsification_assessment: OVERSTATED / PARTIALLY UNSUPPORTED. Conflates joint protocol differences with isolated causal mechanisms.
scientifically_defensible_replacement: The historical negative interaction is highly sensitive to protocol specification; eliminating truncation censoring and matching prompt prefix lengths dissolves the interaction, though the isolated contribution of each factor remains empirically confounded.

historical_claim_wording: Language models possess an intrinsic inability to self-correct reasoning errors (recovery rate = 0%).
original_scientific_flaw: Generalizes from a continuation task terminating with "Step 2: Calculate..." to all reasoning paradigms.
empirical_evidence_status: CONDITIONALLY SUPPORTED ONLY IN SPECIFIC CONTINUATION SETTING.
falsification_assessment: OVERGENERALIZED CONSTRUCT. Conflates continuation inertia under prefill entrainment with general cognitive incapacity.
scientifically_defensible_replacement: Under autoregressive continuation without critique cues, 1.5B models display complete continuation inertia, propagating injected intermediate errors into downstream calculations in 98.5% of cases.

historical_claim_wording: The Base model achieves 97% Control accuracy while Instruct achieves 100%, demonstrating that instruction tuning improves baseline accuracy by 3%.
original_scientific_flaw: Attributed a 3% gap to model competence when it was caused by a heuristic parser extracting the step index (3) from trailing text.
empirical_evidence_status: FALSIFIED BY TRACE AUDIT. The 3 disputed Base rollouts were mathematically 100% correct.
falsification_assessment: PARSER ARTIFACT. Both Base and Instruct achieve 100% mathematical accuracy on unperturbed Control prefixes.
scientifically_defensible_replacement: Both base and instruct models achieve 100% mathematical accuracy on unperturbed control prefixes under semantic evaluation; the apparent 3% gap under heuristic parsing is an artifact of conversational verbosity.
